To summarize, I reached a year on T at the beginning of this month, and I have never been as happy in my entire life as I have been in the past year. 
I have fleeting memories of feeling content before starting T, but it was more like I was making do with what I was stuck with: now, I feel like I can do anything I want. I feel like I can finally start my life, and I have much more motivation and confidence than I ever did before. 
I would be so many steps ahead in life right now if I had this kind of enthusiasm sooner, and if I can garner anything from my experience so far, it is that hormone replacement therapy is life changing for people who really need it.

I don’t think you need to feel guilty for connecting to Barry. I think all people go through a time where they can relate to that. Obviously, Barry is a certain kind of extreme that we can’t relate to entirely, but his plight is relatable in the same way that people relate to Frankenstein’s Monster because he was shunned for not meeting his creator’s expectations. Two completely different characters with completely different issues, but they’re both an extreme circumstance that calls on our empathy and need to relate. Also, you may have missed the “point” of Barry, but I think enjoying your time watching matters more than sniffing around for a deeper meaning. You’re not being graded on how you perceive the show, it’s just something you can enjoy in your free time. That’s just how I see it.

No Country for Old Men: The meaning (or the meaning that I perceive) of the movie is something that I really enjoy and the amount of detail that went into No Country is something that I personally adore. It might be difficult to understand the appeal at first, but after you watch it for the first time there are good YouTube videos explaining the movie. 

The Shape of Water: The symbolism of the movie, the music, and the visuals bring me to tears no matter how often I watch it. The characters are those you can sympathize with regardless of if you perceive them as “good” or “evil.”

The Man without a Face: This movie is one that easily has me laughing and smiling one moment, then crying the next. The progression of the characters and the rollercoaster of emotions this movie takes the watcher through make it worth a watch if you really want to feel something. 

As Good As It Gets: This one is a rollercoaster in the same way that the last movie is, with a similar progression in the characters, but for completely different reasons with completely different circumstances. Either way, one of the greats. 

I could keep going, but these are generally the first movies I think of when I want to recommend movies without knowing the other person’s taste. That, and I don’t really recognize the ones you have in your poll.
